name: Costing
lineup: Supplier invoices arrive on their own and get matched to the job. Confirm with one keystroke and the cost posts to your CRM before your coffee's cold.

seo.title: Costing — Kickback
seo.description: Costing pulls supplier invoices in every day, matches each one to a job in your CRM, and posts confirmed costs and invoice PDFs back to that job.
seo.ogDescription: Supplier invoices pulled in daily, matched to the right job, and posted back to your CRM.

hero.headlineHtml: Every supplier invoice on the right job.
hero.lede: Costing pulls invoices from your supplier accounts every day and matches each one to a job in your CRM. You confirm the cost with one key, and it lands on the job with the invoice PDF.

sections.title: Works With
sections.note: Supplier invoices for material costs. Gusto payroll for labor.

sections.title: Invoice to Job Cost
sections.lede: Connect your CRM and your supplier accounts once. After that, every invoice goes through the same three steps.

items.title: Invoices Arrive
items.body: Costing pulls new invoices from your supplier accounts every day. Home Depot and Lowe's order emails can also be forwarded straight in.

items.title: Auto-Match Finds the Job
items.body: It checks each invoice's PO against your jobs' numbers, addresses, customer names and dates. Clear matches get linked to the job. The rest wait in your Invoice Inbox with the three likeliest jobs.

items.title: Costs Land on the Job
items.bodyHtml: Pick the cost line and press <kbd>Enter</kbd>. The invoice total posts to the job in your CRM. The invoice PDF is already on that job, attached when the invoice was linked, if the supplier provides one.

items.title: Invoices Come In by Themselves
items.body: Connect each supplier account once. Every day Costing signs in, pulls the new invoices and grabs the PDF where the supplier has one. Nobody has to log into portals or dig through email to find them.

bullets.title: Direct Connections
bullets.text: Sherwin-Williams, Associated Materials and Wincore sync straight from the supplier's system with your account login.

bullets.title: Portal Pulls
bullets.text: Spectrum Paint and The Home Depot are read from their websites with your saved login. If a portal asks for a one-time code, you finish signing in from Kickback.

bullets.title: Email Forwarding
bullets.text: Home Depot and Lowe's order emails forwarded to your connection's address show up without waiting for the daily sync.

bullets.title: Sync Any Time
bullets.text: Press Sync for an extra pull, or run a Full Historical Sync to bring in older invoices.

items.title: Auto-Match
items.bodyHtml: Auto-Match compares every new invoice with the jobs opened around its date. When the PO matches a job number, or one job is a clear fit, it links the invoice to that job on its own. Close calls wait in the Invoice Inbox, which runs on the keyboard: <kbd>J</kbd> and <kbd>K</kbd> move through the queue, <kbd>1</kbd> to <kbd>3</kbd> pick a job, <kbd>Enter</kbd> confirms, <kbd>S</kbd> searches, and <kbd>O</kbd> or <kbd>I</kbd> marks an invoice overhead or ignored.

bullets.title: Linked Invoices Arrive Ready
bullets.text: Invoices it linked show up with the job set and a cost line already picked. Press Enter to post it.

bullets.title: Every Guess Shows Its Reason
bullets.text: Each suggested job is tagged with what lined up: the PO, the job address, the customer name or the job dates.

bullets.title: Daily Auto-Match Digest
bullets.text: One email a day lists the invoices Auto-Match linked in the last 24 hours, with a link to undo any of them. Owners pick the hour, and nothing is sent on days it linked none.

items.title: Labor Costing From Payroll
items.body: Connect Gusto and payroll payments come in every day, or upload a payments report exported from Gusto. Open a payment, split it across the jobs it covered by dollar amount, and each share posts to that job in your CRM as a labor line.

bullets.title: Suggested Jobs
bullets.text: Costing lists the jobs that person was assigned to around the pay date, with the unsplit balance already filled in.

bullets.title: Changed Payments Get Flagged
bullets.text: If payroll changes a payment you already split, it moves to Needs Review so you can check the split again.

bullets.title: Removals Carry Over
bullets.text: Take a share off a job and its labor line comes off the job in your CRM too.

items.title: Data Integrity
items.body: Costing also checks the cost lines already on your jobs and sorts the problems into three lists. Delete a line in Kickback and it's gone from your CRM too.

bullets.title: Duplicates
bullets.text: Copies of a cost line on the same job, side by side with the differences highlighted. Keep one and delete the rest.

bullets.title: Zero Cost Items
bullets.text: Cost lines sitting on a job at $0.00.

bullets.title: Unlinked Items
bullets.text: Cost lines with no supplier invoice behind them.

sections.title: Automatic vs. You Confirm
sections.lede: Auto-Match decides which job an invoice belongs to. A person decides what changes the costs on that job.

sections.title: Works With Your Other Apps
sections.lede: Costing shares its CRM and supplier connections with the rest of Kickback, so you connect each account once.

items.body: Connect Associated Materials or Wincore once and it feeds both apps. Costing reads each order as an invoice, and Warehouse tracks the delivery for the same job.
Both apps run on the same CRM connection. Follow-Up chases your open estimates, and Costing tracks what the won jobs cost.

items.q: Will it change my job costs without asking?
items.a: No. Auto-Match links invoices to jobs and attaches the PDF. A cost line goes on a job only when someone on your team confirms it.

items.q: What if Auto-Match picks the wrong job?
items.a: Undo it from the daily digest or from the Auto-Matched view in the inbox. The invoice goes back in the queue for you to match by hand.

items.q: Do I still have to log into supplier portals?
items.a: Only to connect each account, and when a portal asks for a one-time code. Costing handles the daily sign-in after that.

items.q: What labor cost does it use?
items.a: The gross pay on each payroll payment. Employer taxes and hours aren't pulled in, and a person decides how each payment splits across jobs.

items.q: Will it work with my CRM?
items.a: Ask when you book a demo. Kickback sets up every account, so you'll know before you start.
